plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC's new Physiotherapy Services Agreement for musculoskeletal (MSK) physiotherapy took effect April 1, 2026.
exact_quote_or_summary: "The WorkSafeBC website has been updated, and the following documents related to the April 1, 2026 services agreement launch are now available."
notes: Companion docs posted: Physiotherapy Services Agreement, Physiotherapy Fee Schedule, Physiotherapy Services Reference Manual. Use only as an 'as of April 1, 2026' context line.

plain_language_claim: The previous WorkSafeBC physiotherapy services contract expired March 14, 2026; services given on or before March 31, 2026 fall under that old contract.
exact_quote_or_summary: "The Contractor acknowledges and agrees that any Services provided on or before March 31, 2026 will be subject to and governed by the terms of the applicable physiotherapy services contract that expired March 14, 2026."
notes: Transition rule. Provider-internal, no value to workers.

plain_language_claim: Existing contracted physiotherapy clinics were sent the new agreement to review and accept; they were not automatically carried over.
exact_quote_or_summary: "All current physiotherapy providers have now received their copy of the new Physiotherapy Services Agreement for review and consideration."
notes: Quote is KNOWN; the reading that each clinic had to sign the new agreement to stay contracted is an ASSUMPTION. No source says whether incumbents had to re-apply. This is why Synergy's 2026 contract status must be confirmed by staff (see SYN-01).

plain_language_claim: The Physiotherapy Services Reference Manual (February 2026) is used with the Physiotherapy Services Memorandum of Agreement and schedules effective April 1, 2026.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: manual is meant to be used with the Physiotherapy Services Memorandum of Agreement, including amendments and related schedules, effective April 1, 2026.
notes: Name of the new contract per WorkSafeBC: 'Physiotherapy Services Agreement' / 'Physiotherapy Services Memorandum of Agreement'. New contract number: Not Available (the agreement document surfaced shows Contract 89088, which looks like the expired template).

plain_language_claim: From April 1, 2026 clinics must use new report forms: Initial Report 83D555 (R26/04) and a combined Physiotherapy Treatment Report 83D665 (R26/04) that replaces the separate Extension Request and Discharge reports.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Please transition to these versions before April 1, 2026, after which old templates should no longer be used"; 83D665 replaces the Extension Request and Discharge Reports.
notes: Ops item for clinic staff (old form 83D219 retired). Not worker copy.

plain_language_claim: Bulletin 2026-29 (March 30, 2026) clarified billing: the Complex Fee (code 19109) only applies to visits given by a physical therapist (not KIN/PTSW); the Clinical Administrative Fee may be billed only once per claim.
source_date_or_retrieved: Bulletin dated 2026-03-30 per WebSearch summary; retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: "The Complex Fee can only be invoiced for treatment visits provided directly by a Physical Therapist. It cannot be provided by a KIN or PTSW." (snippet via standard WebSearch)
notes: Bulletin text itself was not surfaced by the domain-restricted extended search; companion Key Clarifications FAQ (published 2026-03-23) exists at https://www.worksafebc.com/en/resources/health-care-providers/guides/physiotherapy-services-agreement-key-clarifications-faq?lang=en&direct

plain_language_claim: New clinics join the WorkSafeBC MSK physiotherapy network by emailing Vendor Application Form 19D210 (R26/04) to procurement@worksafebc.com; one form per legal entity; WorkSafeBC intends to award contracts to clinics that meet the requirements.
exact_quote_or_summary: "It is WorkSafeBC's intention to award contracts to clinics that meet the application requirements." Applicants must operate a clinic in B.C. with a registered physiotherapist (CHCPBC).
notes: Requirements (LIKELY, summaries): privacy/FIPPA, accessible facility (2025 form), alternate physiotherapists, PT orientation seminars, employer registration in good standing. EAPP is requested on the same form.

plain_language_claim: Since January 1, 2026 WorkSafeBC chiropractic care runs on individual chiropractor contracts; all chiropractors, including those under the former agreement, must apply.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: new chiropractic services agreement effective January 1, 2026; contracting moved from the BC Chiropractic Association agreement to individual provider contracts.
notes: An older 'Becoming a provider' page says no contract is needed (outdated). Synergy Jane shows no WCB chiropractic appointment types (research/04, KNOWN). Do not claim WorkSafeBC chiropractic at Synergy until each chiropractor's contract is confirmed.

plain_language_claim: PABC (Physiotherapy Association of BC) negotiated changes to the WorkSafe Physiotherapy Service Agreement and expects further changes in the next agreement.
exact_quote_or_summary: "after several months of negotiations, PABC and WorkSafe are addressing important changes to the Physiotherapy Service Agreement"
notes: Industry context only. The 2022 PABC article (https://bcphysio.org/news-and-publications/pabc-news/new-worksafebc-contract) describes the previous contract (fee-for-service, $83/visit then); outdated.

plain_language_claim: If you need physiotherapy for a work injury, go to a WorkSafeBC-contracted physiotherapist in your region and tell them the injury is work-related.
source_date_or_retrieved: retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet); page date not shown (search metadata ~2 years, but page carries April 1, 2026 rate)
exact_quote_or_summary: "If you need physiotherapy, you should visit one of the service providers who have a contract with us in your region. Be sure to explain that your injury is work-related."
notes: Best official basis for 'go straight to a contracted physio'.

plain_language_claim: At a contracted physiotherapist you can get an initial assessment even before WorkSafeBC accepts your claim, and the clinic bills WorkSafeBC directly for that assessment.
exact_quote_or_summary: "By choosing one of our contracted physiotherapists, you can get an initial assessment even before we accept your claim. They will bill us directly for this assessment."
notes: General rule is publishable. Saying Synergy clinics do this depends on SYN-01 (2026 contract status).

plain_language_claim: A contracted physio can do the initial assessment without prior WorkSafeBC approval on a pending or accepted claim if it happens within 60 days of the injury (or of claim-related surgery).
exact_quote_or_summary: Manual: "The Physiotherapy Initial Assessment (or the Post-Surgical Physiotherapy Initial Assessment) is allowed on a pending or accepted claim without prior approval from the claim owner provided the assessment occurs within 60 days of the date of injury or the date of claim-related surgery." Provider page: "You can perform an initial assessment within 60 days of the injury for any worker who has an accepted or pending claim with us."
notes: This is the '60-day direct-access window'. It is about the assessment needing no pre-approval, not about eligibility ending.

plain_language_claim: You need a WorkSafeBC claim (it can still be pending) for the clinic to bill WorkSafeBC, so report the injury to WorkSafeBC before or when you book.
exact_quote_or_summary: "...for any worker who has an accepted or pending claim with us."
notes: Inference (LIKELY): 'pending claim' means the injury has been reported and a claim exists. No source quoted on whether a clinic may assess a worker who has not yet reported. Plain-language wording should say 'report your injury to WorkSafeBC'.

plain_language_claim: If treatment starts more than 60 days after the injury, WorkSafeBC must approve it first (it is not automatically refused).
exact_quote_or_summary: "If the injured worker starts treatment more than 60 calendar days after the date of injury, pre-approval is required before providing services."
notes: Contradicts Synergy wording that frames 60 days as an eligibility cut-off (SYN-04).

plain_language_claim: The treatment period can start without prior approval if it begins within 30 days of the initial assessment or within 60 days of the injury.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary of manual: treatment period can start without prior approval if it begins within 30 days of the initial assessment or within 60 days of the date of injury.
notes: Not quoted verbatim; check live manual.

plain_language_claim: No doctor's referral is needed for WorkSafeBC physiotherapy.
exact_quote_or_summary: No official snippet states this for physiotherapy. Official worker page sends workers straight to a contracted physio (WSBC-10). Benefits page says a referral IS required for massage therapy and NOT required for chiropractic, acupuncture and naturopathy (summary).
notes: LIKELY true (no referral requirement found anywhere for physio). Publish the WSBC-10 wording instead of an absolute 'no referral needed'.

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC-funded treatment visits (beyond the initial assessment) start only once the claim is accepted.
exact_quote_or_summary: "the Physiotherapy Treatment Period cannot commence before the Injured Worker's claim is accepted by WorkSafeBC."
notes: Quote may come from the expired contract text, but the Feb 2026 manual repeats that the treatment period is only available on an accepted claim (summary).

plain_language_claim: Under the April 2026 rules the first treatment period is up to 10 visits or 5 calendar weeks, whichever comes first (physio treatments and kinesiology/PT support worker sessions combined), unless WorkSafeBC directs fewer.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Includes up to 10 visits (PT Treatment and/or PTSW/KIN Support Sessions) or five calendar weeks of treatments, whichever is reached earlier, unless a WorkSafeBC officer directs fewer treatments are indicated." Table: "Treatment Period 10 visits 5 weeks".
notes: Quote is KNOWN, but official sources disagree: the agreement document surfaced (Contract 89088, expired template), the 2022 billing guide, the flowchart and an invoicing page indexed recently still say 15 visits / 6 weeks (WSBC-19). The manual is the only 2026-dated source. Confirm against the signed 2026 agreement schedule before printing a number.

plain_language_claim: Old rule (pre-April 2026): up to 15 visits or 6 calendar weeks per treatment period.
source_date_or_retrieved: Billing guide dt=2022-12-07; agreement term ended 2026-03-14; retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: "The Contractor shall provide up to 15 visits or six calendar weeks of treatments, whichever is reached earlier, unless a Board Officer directs fewer treatments are indicated, in a Physiotherapy Treatment Period." Billing guide: "A treatment period consists of 15 visits or 6 weeks of treatment, whichever occurs first."
notes: Superseded by WSBC-18 (LIKELY). Synergy still publishes 15/6 (SYN-03). Some WorkSafeBC pages still show 15/6, so WorkSafeBC's own site is internally inconsistent.

plain_language_claim: Extensions: a standard extension is up to 8 visits or 4 weeks; an extended extension of up to 16 visits or 8 weeks applies to certain listed injury types; WorkSafeBC must approve before an extension starts.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Standard Extension: 8 visits, 4 weeks; Extended Extension: 16 visits, 8 weeks." "WorkSafeBC officer approval is required, prior to starting an extension."
notes: Quoted from manual table; not confirmed against the agreement schedule.

plain_language_claim: Your physiotherapist can ask WorkSafeBC for more treatment if you need it; WorkSafeBC decides whether to approve it.
exact_quote_or_summary: "WorkSafeBC officer approval is required, prior to starting an extension." "WorkSafeBC has the right in its sole discretion to approve or decline a request for an Extension."
notes: Request goes on the 83D665 Treatment Report at least 7 days before the period ends and no earlier than the third calendar week (summary). Keep worker copy at this plain level.

plain_language_claim: Only one WorkSafeBC treatment visit per day per claim; a kinesiology or PT support worker session cannot be billed the same day as a physio treatment visit.
exact_quote_or_summary: "A KIN/PTSW session cannot be billed on the same day as a PT Treatment Visit for the same claim."
notes: Scheduling rule for front desk.

plain_language_claim: Once WorkSafeBC accepts your claim, your provider bills WorkSafeBC for claim-related services and you should not have to pay any fees.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Once we accept your claim, your health care provider should bill us for any services related to your claim. You should not have to pay any fees."
notes: Core 'no cost' line. Applies to services related to the accepted claim.

plain_language_claim: Contracted physio clinics may not charge injured workers extra (no top-ups or user fees) for services under the WorkSafeBC agreement, except where the agreement expressly allows.
exact_quote_or_summary: "The Contractor shall not charge directly or indirectly any fees or other charges of any nature for Services provided under this Agreement to the Injured Worker or to any other individual, business or other entity, except as expressly permitted in this Agreement."
notes: KNOWN quote, but it may come from the expired contract text. Very LIKELY carried into the 2026 agreement. Manual also bars charging for basic clinic / non-durable supplies (summary).

plain_language_claim: Treatment of body areas that are not part of the accepted claim can be billed to the worker.
exact_quote_or_summary: Massage guide: "the injured worker is responsible for the payment for treatment for nonclaim related areas."
notes: Quoted for massage only; physio equivalent not quoted.

plain_language_claim: If you choose a physiotherapist who is not contracted with WorkSafeBC, you pay for the visit and claim it back at WorkSafeBC's rate ($95 per visit from April 1, 2026); you pay any difference.
exact_quote_or_summary: "If you choose a physiotherapist who is not contracted with us, you will have to pay for your visit. You can then seek reimbursement from us. Please keep in mind that we will reimburse you at established rates and you will be responsible for any difference." "Physiotherapy | $95 per visit (effective April 1, 2026)"
notes: Only relevant to non-contracted clinics. Do not use on Synergy pages in a way that suggests Synergy patients pay a gap.

plain_language_claim: 2026 contracted fee schedule: initial assessment $196, treatment visit $95, KIN session $70, PTSW session $65, complex fee $115 (max 4 per claim).
source_date_or_retrieved: Fee schedule published 2026-03-31 (search metadata); retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary of a garbled fee table (codes 19100/19101, 19102, 19107, 19108, 19109). Dates of service April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, CPI after.
notes: Provider-internal pricing. Code labels (19100 vs 19101) unclear in snippet.

plain_language_claim: If you get physio before your claim is accepted, the clinic may ask you to pay; if the claim is accepted later, you can ask the clinic for a refund.
exact_quote_or_summary: "If you get medical treatments (e.g., physiotherapy) related to your claim before it's accepted, you may be asked to pay the provider directly. If your claim is later accepted, you can contact your treatment provider to request reimbursement."
notes: Synergy's own pending-claim payment policy must be stated next to this (SYN-10).

plain_language_claim: If your claim is pending at your first visit, WorkSafeBC pays the contracted clinic for the initial assessment even if the claim is later denied.
exact_quote_or_summary: "If the claim is pending at the time of the Initial Assessment, you can bill the Initial Assessment fee code, which will be paid even if the claim is subsequently disallowed."
notes: Covers the initial assessment only, and the clinic must file the initial report within 7 days for payment (83D555).

plain_language_claim: If the claim is denied, WorkSafeBC does not pay for treatment given while the claim was pending; the clinic decides whether to collect from the worker or wait for the decision.
exact_quote_or_summary: "it's up to you how payment is collected (i.e., directly from the injured worker or waiting until a claim decision is made before continuing to treat)"; "if the claim is subsequently disallowed, we will not pay for treatment provided during this pending time."
notes: Rule is official. What Synergy actually does (charge privately vs wait) is a business decision staff must confirm before publishing.

plain_language_claim: If a pending claim is accepted within 60 days of the initial assessment, the clinic must refund the worker in full and bill WorkSafeBC; after that, WorkSafeBC reimburses the worker.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: if acceptance comes within 60 days of the initial assessment, the worker must be reimbursed in full for amounts paid before acceptance and the clinic invoices WorkSafeBC (Schedule B rates). Agreement sets a 90-day invoicing window.
notes: Not quoted verbatim; timelines need a check against the live manual.

plain_language_claim: Under EAPP, if the claim is denied or suspended WorkSafeBC still covers the initial assessment but further treatment becomes the employer's responsibility.
source_date_or_retrieved: retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet); page ~13 months old per metadata
exact_quote_or_summary: "In this case, the initial assessment will be covered by WorkSafeBC but any additional treatments will be the responsibility of the employer."
notes: Employer-program rule only (EAPP). Not for general worker pages.

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC publishes regional lists of physiotherapy clinics contracted for musculoskeletal care (e.g., Metro Vancouver, Fraser Valley).
exact_quote_or_summary: "musculoskeletal physiotherapy providers who are contracted with WorkSafeBC"; list header "WorkSafeBC Authorized Physiotherapy Providers List".
notes: The task's target URL (.../musculoskeletal-physiotherapy-services/contracted-musculoskeletal-physiotherapy-provider-lists) did not surface; a sitecore variant (.../physiotherapists/contracted-physiotherapy-provider-lists) did. Indexed copies are ~16-23 months old (pre-April 2026).

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC keeps separate provider lists for EAPP, concussion/vestibular physio, chiropractic, hand therapy and Return to Work Support Services.
exact_quote_or_summary: List titles in results: 'Early Access to Physiotherapy Program (EAPP) Providers', 'Concussion & vestibular physiotherapy provider list', 'Chiropractic services providers list', 'Hand Therapy Program service providers'.
notes: Being on one list does not mean being on another.

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC massage therapy needs a doctor's referral and an accepted claim; it covers an initial assessment plus up to 6 treatments in the first 8 weeks from the injury without pre-approval; more needs approval.
exact_quote_or_summary: "The injured worker must have an accepted claim with us. A doctor's referral is required for you to begin treating an injured worker." "You can provide an initial assessment and up to six treatments within the first eight weeks from the date of injury without pre-approval."
notes: Synergy shows 'WCB Massage Subsequent Session' at 9 clinics (research/04, KNOWN). RMT contract status per clinic UNKNOWN; massage services agreement Contract #81664 (amended and renewed) exists.

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC acupuncture: accepted claim, no referral, no prior approval if clinically indicated with an active-rehab focus; up to 8 visits in 8 weeks, then a Board Officer must approve.
source_date_or_retrieved: Acupuncture fee schedule dated 2026-02-01; retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: "The injured worker must have an accepted claim with us. Services are clinically indicated for the accepted injury and there is a focus on active rehabilitation and return to work." 8 visits / 8 weeks from fee schedule (summary).
notes: Nordel offers WCB Acupuncture types in Jane (research/04, KNOWN). Confirm acupuncturist's WorkSafeBC status.

plain_language_claim: Chiropractic for WorkSafeBC claims needs no referral.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: benefits page states chiropractor, acupuncture and naturopath patients do not need a referral for treatment.
notes: Not quoted verbatim. See WSBC-08 on chiropractor contracts.

plain_language_claim: Providers who do not bill WorkSafeBC directly are reimbursed to the worker at $72 per visit (from January 1, 2026) for chiropractic, massage and acupuncture.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary only.
notes: Not needed for Synergy pages.

plain_language_claim: From April 1, 2026, kinesiologist (KIN) and physical therapist support worker (PTSW) sessions can be part of the WorkSafeBC physio treatment period, count toward the visit allocation and stay under the treating physio's oversight.
exact_quote_or_summary: "these will count towards the injured worker's allocated treatment visits within the Treatment Period." "Each Support Session must be at least 45 minutes, with 30 minutes spent 1:1."
notes: There is no stand-alone WorkSafeBC kinesiology benefit a worker can book directly in what was found. Fee schedule snippet implies 45 min one-on-one; manual says 45 min with 30 min 1:1 (minor conflict). Confirm Synergy uses KIN support sessions under WCB before mentioning.

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC merged OR1, OR2 and ASTD into one Customized Recovery and Return-to-Work Program from November 1, 2024; OR1 remains only in rural or more remote communities.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary of announcement: OR1, OR2 and ASTD consolidated into the Customized Recovery and Return-to-Work Program effective November 1, 2024.
notes: Program needs WorkSafeBC approval and approved providers. Synergy not seen on RTWSS provider list (LIKELY). Do not imply Synergy runs these programs.

plain_language_claim: Early Access to Physiotherapy Program (EAPP) is employer-arranged: the employer has a return-to-work program and partners with a pre-approved EAPP clinic; the worker reports to a supervisor or first aid within 72 hours and opens a claim.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Reports the injury to their supervisor or first aid attendant within 72 hours. Contacts WorkSafeBC and establishes a claim." "select a pre-approved EAPP physiotherapy clinic (or clinics) to set up a provider agreement and partnership"
notes: Synergy clinics appear on EAPP lists (LIKELY). Fits an employer-facing section only.

plain_language_claim: After a work injury: get first aid or care, tell your employer as soon as it is safe, and tell any health provider the injury happened at work.
exact_quote_or_summary: "let your employer know about your injury as soon as it is safe to do so"; "If you receive medical attention, tell whoever treats you that the injury happened at work."

plain_language_claim: Report the injury to WorkSafeBC online (24/7, recommended for a physical injury from a single incident) or by phone through Teleclaim.
exact_quote_or_summary: "You can report your injury online 24 hours a day, 7 days a week." Phone suits mental health injuries, hearing loss, gradual-onset injuries, occupational disease and similar.
notes: Phone report usually takes about 30 minutes (summary).

plain_language_claim: Teleclaim: 604.231.8888 (Lower Mainland) or 1.888.967.5377 toll-free, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific.
exact_quote_or_summary: "Claims Call Centre / Teleclaim Phone: 604.231.8888 Toll-free: 1.888.967.5377"; Contact Us: "Monday - Friday 8:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m."
notes: The task's 1-888-967-5377 is correct. Note: one summary also tied 1-888-967-5377 to the Prevention Information Line; do not use it for that.

plain_language_claim: You have up to one year from the date of injury to report it to WorkSafeBC, but should report right away.
exact_quote_or_summary: "You do have up to one year from the date you were injured to report it to us."

plain_language_claim: WorkSafeBC sends an 8-digit claim number by mail once it receives your report.
exact_quote_or_summary: "an 8-digit number that you'll get by mail once we receive your injury report"

plain_language_claim: Employers must report within 72 hours when a worker misses time or needs medical care beyond first aid.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: employers must report within 72 hours if a worker missed time from work or required medical attention beyond first aid.
notes: Not quoted verbatim.

plain_language_claim: The paper/fax Form 6 is retired; workers report online or by phone.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary: the fax and mail version of Form 6 has been retired.
notes: Do not tell workers to 'fill out Form 6'.

plain_language_claim: Have ready: your and your employer's contact details, Personal Health Number, when and how the injury happened, first medical visit details; earnings for the past 12 weeks and SIN if you missed work.
exact_quote_or_summary: Summary of the 'what to have ready' list.
notes: Link to the official page rather than reproducing the list.

plain_language_claim: All Synergy Rehab clinics are WorkSafeBC-contracted MSK physiotherapy providers under the April 1, 2026 agreement.
source_date_or_retrieved: Lists indexed ~2024 to early 2025; retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: Synergy Rehab rows appear in cached Metro Vancouver / Fraser Valley physio lists and EAPP lists (LIKELY), but no list dated after April 1, 2026 was found. Jane shows WCB Physio Initial/Subsequent types at all 19 clinics (research/04, KNOWN).
notes: Gate for every 'WorkSafeBC-contracted' or 'direct billing' claim. Staff to confirm the signed 2026 agreement and WorkSafeBC vendor/payee numbers per clinic.

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages: '10 sessions are scheduled over 5 weeks' / 'pre-authorized allowance of 10 physiotherapy sessions' (/worksafe-physiotherapy/, homepage).
source_date_or_retrieved: Synergy text LIKELY (research/02); rule retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: Official (manual): up to 10 combined visits or 5 calendar weeks, whichever first, officer may direct fewer, KIN/PTSW sessions count, accepted claims only.
notes: Number now matches the 2026 manual, but 'allowance' and 'scheduled' overstate it. Rewrite as 'up to 10 visits or 5 weeks, whichever comes first' after WSBC-18 is confirmed. Source page: https://synergyrehabilitation.ca/worksafe-physiotherapy/

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages: '15 sessions are scheduled over 6 weeks' / 'initial authorization for up to 15 physiotherapy sessions' (/icbc-claims/, 2023 social graphic, King George and Delta location pages).
source_date_or_retrieved: Synergy text KNOWN on /icbc-claims/ (research/02); rule retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: 15 visits / 6 weeks is the expired pre-April-2026 contract figure (WSBC-19).
notes: Remove or update everywhere. Source page: https://synergyrehabilitation.ca/icbc-claims/

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages: 'Approved claims are eligible for treatment within 60 days of your injury or accident'.
source_date_or_retrieved: Synergy text KNOWN on /icbc-claims/; retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: the 60-day window is when the initial assessment (pending or accepted claim) or treatment start needs no pre-approval; after 60 days WorkSafeBC pre-approval is required (WSBC-12, WSBC-14).
notes: Misleading: implies no coverage after 60 days and only for approved claims. Rewrite.

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages: 'Additional sessions may be requested as part of your treatment plan'.
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: extensions need WorkSafeBC officer approval before starting (WSBC-20, WSBC-21).
notes: OK if it adds 'WorkSafeBC decides'.

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages / Yelp: 'You do not need a doctor's referral to start WorkSafe physiotherapy for most cases'.
exact_quote_or_summary: No official text found that requires a referral for physio; none found that says 'no referral' explicitly either (WSBC-16).
notes: 'For most cases' is vague. Use WSBC-10 wording. Never extend 'no referral' to massage (WSBC-35).

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages: report the injury to WorkSafeBC first, get a claim number, bring it to the first appointment.
exact_quote_or_summary: Consistent with WSBC-42 to WSBC-46. Official rules also allow the assessment while the claim is pending.
notes: Add 'tell your employer' and 'your claim can still be pending'.

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages / Jane: 'we bill WorkSafeBC directly' / 'Direct billing to ICBC, WCB & most extended health plans'.
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: contracted physios bill WorkSafeBC directly (WSBC-11, WSBC-23).
notes: True only if SYN-01 is confirmed. Bodyworker, personal training and 'No Direct Billing' disciplines are not WorkSafe services (research/04).

plain_language_claim: Synergy pages / Jane: 'No user fees for ICBC + WorkSafeBC accepted' / 'no out-of-pocket expenses for approved treatments' / 'you pay nothing'.
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: accepted claim, claim-related services, no fees (WSBC-23); contractor may not charge extra (WSBC-24). Exceptions: treatment while pending (WSBC-28/30), non-claim body areas (WSBC-25), services WorkSafeBC does not cover.
notes: Keep, but qualify with 'on an accepted claim, for your claim-related injury'. Depends on SYN-01.

plain_language_claim: Synergy blog: 'You also do not have to wait for that acceptance letter.'
source_date_or_retrieved: Synergy text KNOWN (blog meta, research/02); retrieved 2026-11-02 (WebSearch snippet)
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: true for the initial assessment at a contracted clinic within 60 days; treatment visits while pending are not WorkSafeBC-funded unless the claim is accepted, and the clinic may charge the worker meanwhile (WSBC-28 to WSBC-31).
notes: Needs the pending-claim payment policy next to it. Source: https://synergyrehabilitation.ca/worksafebc-physiotherapy-what-is-covered/

plain_language_claim: Synergy blog: WorkSafeBC pays only 'its established rate' and the patient covers any gap.
exact_quote_or_summary: Official: the 'established rate, you pay the difference' rule applies to NON-contracted providers (WSBC-26). Contracted clinics may not top up (WSBC-24).
notes: Contradicts SYN-09 if Synergy is contracted. Remove or reframe as a non-contracted-clinic warning.

plain_language_claim: Synergy Jane bio (South Surrey): physiotherapist ran 'WorkSafeBC (OR1 & OR2)' multidisciplinary programs.
exact_quote_or_summary: OR1/OR2/ASTD consolidated into the Customized Recovery and Return-to-Work Program from November 1, 2024 (WSBC-40).
notes: Fine as past experience; must not read as a current Synergy WorkSafeBC program. Edit bio to past tense.

plain_language_claim: Synergy blog: massage needs a physician referral; up to 6 massage treatments within 8 weeks; chiropractic and acupuncture need no referral.
exact_quote_or_summary: Massage part matches WSBC-35 (VERIFIED). Chiro/acupuncture no-referral PARTIAL (WSBC-36, WSBC-37). Chiropractors now need individual contracts (WSBC-08).
notes: Massage line OK. Do not present WorkSafeBC chiropractic as available until confirmed.

plain_language_claim: Synergy blog: WorkSafeBC pays mileage for claim trips over 20 km one way.
exact_quote_or_summary: Not checked against an official source in this session.
notes: Leave out until verified on the WorkSafeBC travel/expense page.

plain_language_claim: Synergy blog: 'there is no single fixed number published for every claim' (visits).
exact_quote_or_summary: Official manual publishes a standard allocation (10 visits / 5 weeks) and extension sizes, and the officer may direct fewer.
notes: Partly true but contradicts the site's own 10/5 copy. Harmonize to one confirmed wording.

plain_language_claim: Medimap listing 'Synergy Rehabilitation Inc.' (120-12852 96 Ave, Surrey = Cedar Hills) lists payment as private insurance and credit card, with no WorkSafeBC/WCB.
exact_quote_or_summary: Third-party listing omits WCB while Jane shows WCB physio types at Cedar Hills (research/04, KNOWN).
